$comment: The only place a hostname is written. app/core/cors.py builds the credentialed-request allowlist from these, and the frontends need the api host BAKED IN at build time as VITE_API_ORIGIN, so a host change here means setting that variable and rebuilding the three apps. **All four hosts in an environment MUST share one registrable domain.** The refresh cookie is SameSite=Lax and host-only, so a browser will not send it across sites -- and `up.railway.app` is on the Public Suffix List, which makes every Railway hostname its own site. Production on Railway hostnames therefore could not hold a session at all: sign-in completed, the cookie was set on the api's host, the browser refused to send it back, and the app returned to its sign-in screen in a loop. That is what the custom domains are FOR; they are not cosmetic. Production moved to them 2026-08-30.
$comment_apex: #25 (2026-09-08) -- the club's landing page answers at the APEX and at www, not only under app. Both are extra ORIGINS on the parent app, never a replacement for it: `app_origin` must keep naming exactly one reachable host per app, because that is where OAuth returns a signed-in user and a redirect to a second name for the same service is a coin toss. So they live here, where `allowed_origins` widens what the API ACCEPTS without widening where it SENDS people. All three share the registrable domain `gladiatorclub.co.il`, so the host-only SameSite=Lax refresh cookie is unaffected. Removal condition: none -- unlike a mid-migration entry these are permanent, and that is why they are named apart from `transitional_origins`.
